name: Astronautical Apogee Architecture
observations: The codebase uses MCP servers for memory, sequential thinking, and Playwright-based validation, as configured in mcp.json.
Tooling is agent-driven and emphasizes autonomous, iterative improvement with traceable logs.
Configuration files (e.g., mcp.json) are clean, minimal, and workspace-specific.
Strict adherence to project instructions and validation protocols is enforced via MCP servers.
The developer expects all context management, reasoning, and validation to be routed through MCP servers before, during, and after any code or design change.
The codebase is organized for maintainability, extensibility, and composability, with a focus on minimal, reusable structure and atomic CSS.

All memory entity types in the knowledge graph have been reorganized to fit one of the five allowed categories: User, System, Process, Task, Environment, as specified in TODO.md. This ensures strict compliance with project requirements for context management.
Project has grown complex beyond its requirements despite excellent engineering practices.
Current architecture includes 100+ files with 39 TypeScript components and 17 custom web components.
Icon system is fragmented across 16 separate files and needs consolidation.
Theme system is over-engineered with runtime JavaScript switching that could be CSS-native.
Component architecture has over-componentization with minimal code per component.
Global styles file is 500 lines and needs modularization.
GenAIScript automation packages need evaluation for usage patterns and consolidation opportunities.
MCP servers are properly configured for memory, sequential thinking, and Playwright validation.
Development workflow follows strict validation protocols with lint-staged and Husky.
Content management is currently hardcoded and needs data-driven architecture.

The developer's established technique for blog post frontmatter uses a minimal YAML block with triple-dash delimiters and only the fields: id, title, date, and description. This was confirmed by analyzing other blog posts in the workspace.

Tool-specific instructions are now properly separated: memory instructions in memory.instructions.md, Playwright instructions in playwright.instructions.md, sequential thinking instructions in sequential-thinking.instructions.md.
Main copilot-instructions.md now starts with user clarifications section instead of memory requirements, improving logical flow.
Change aligns with user preference for minimal, organized, and efficiently structured instruction files.

2025-08-10: Successfully fixed interstitial icon theme color and positioning issue reported by user.
Problem: Interstitial planet icon was appearing black on white background in top-left corner for split second during page load before JavaScript applied theme variables.

Root cause: CSS variables (--primary-color, --body-background-color) were not available during initial page render before JavaScript theme application, causing SVG to render with no fill color and default positioning.

Solution: Added CSS fallback values using var() function syntax: var(--primary-color, var(--color-sky-600)) for light mode and media query for dark mode with var(--primary-color, var(--color-teal-200)).
Added media query @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) to provide proper dark mode fallbacks when theme variables are not yet loaded.
Background color also given fallback: var(--body-background-color, #fff) for light mode and var(--body-background-color, #0a0a0a) for dark mode.
Testing confirmed: Planet now displays proper theme colors (sky-600 for light, teal-200 for dark) even before JavaScript theme application.
Interstitial remains properly centered in viewport with flexbox centering and correct z-index layering.
Fix follows atomic CSS principles and Andrew's preferences for minimal, composable solutions using existing color system.
Validated with Playwright MCP by simulating CSS variable removal - fallbacks work correctly for both light and dark modes.
